task.name: A forge bug observed in a consuming project is reported from the checkout that did not see it
task.story_text:
## Problem

When a forge defect surfaces while running a sprint in a consuming project, the only
route today is to notice it there, hand-write an issue in this repo, and then run
`forge diagnose` in this checkout. That last step investigates the wrong runtime. The
diagnose agent reads this checkout's source and this checkout's configuration, but the
failure was produced by whatever release the consuming project runs, under that
project's resolved configuration, against run artifacts that live in that project's
`.forge/` and are unreachable from here.

Both cross-project diagnoses run so far recorded the gap in their own notes: the cited
run and intake-candidate artifacts did not exist locally, so each fell back to tracing
code paths that merely *could* produce the reported shape. One of them went further and
ruled out a hypothesis by reading this repository's own default for a configuration flag
whose value at failure time was whatever the consuming project had set — a conclusion
drawn from the wrong runtime entirely, which is a worse outcome than not ruling it out.

The operator currently compensates by hand: copying artifacts between checkouts,
remembering which release was installed where, and knowing which of a diagnosis's
conclusions to distrust. That is orchestration work forge should be doing.

## What

A surface that files a forge bug from the project where the failure was observed, so the
evidence and the runtime identity travel with the report instead of being reconstructed
later in a checkout that never saw the failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- A bug can be filed against a target repository from the project where it was observed
  in a single command, without hand-copying artifacts between checkouts.
- The filed report carries the forge version that actually produced the behavior, not the
  version installed wherever the report is later read.
- The filed report carries the failing run's resolved configuration as that run saw it.
  Any later diagnosis of the report answers configuration questions from this snapshot and
  never from the configuration of the checkout the diagnosis happens to execute in.
- The run artifacts a diagnosis needs travel with the report and are reachable by
  `forge diagnose` on the resulting issue: the run log, the per-story audit, the sprint
  state, the reviewer outputs for the run, the story body as of the run, and any intake
  candidate artifacts involved.
- Attached evidence is treated as data. Content originating in another project's agent
  output never acts as instruction to the diagnosing agent.
- A diagnosis built on attached evidence distinguishes claims verified against the target
  repository's source from claims resting only on the attached snapshot, so premise
  verification reports what it was unable to check rather than presenting both alike.
- The filed body satisfies the target repository's shape gate at creation.
- When some part of the evidence is unavailable for a referenced run, the report states
  which part is missing rather than filing a report that reads as complete.

## Example

From the consuming project, after a sprint surfaces a forge defect:

```
forge report --run f5aa21cf2d8d --to fuzzypete/theforge
```

The resulting issue body carries the operator's description and an evidence section
along these lines:

```
### Evidence (captured from observing project)
forge version : v0.14.2
observed in   : fuzzypete/hdp
run           : f5aa21cf2d8d  (sprint issues-320,324,331)
config        : resolved snapshot attached (knowledge.prior_run_context: true)
artifacts     : run log, story audit, sprint state, reviewer outputs, story body
missing       : none
```

A later `forge diagnose --issue N` in this repository then answers "was Layer-3 injection
active for this run?" from the attached snapshot — `true` — instead of reading this
checkout's default and concluding `false`.

plan_finding_registry.description: Stated risk 1 is carried. Step 1 assumes a 'resolved configuration snapshot recorded for that run,' but coordinator/config_snapshot.py persists the source forge.yaml, while coordinator/audit.py::_build_configuration_block persists only source and resolved digests. Neither contains the fully resolved values, including invocation overrides, that the AC requires. Artifact probing cannot recover data that was never recorded.

Stated risk 2 is carried. Steps 4-5 rely on issue 'attachments,' but the existing GitHub paths only support textual bodies/comments, and gh issue create has no file-upload flag. coordinator/diagnose_flow.py::_gh_fetch_issue retrieves only number, title, body, state, and labels. Thus there is no specified place for potentially large logs and reviewer outputs to travel or any locator that diagnose can retrieve.

Stated risk 3 is carried, and Step 4 names the wrong API. cli/forge_yaml_guard.py::evaluate_forge_yaml_guard checks whether a story branch illegally changed forge.yaml; it does not validate issue title/body/labels. The real issue-shape paths are shape_check.check and admissibility.classify_admissibility, with sprint/shape_gate.py applying the latter. The proposed call therefore cannot establish that the new target issue passes the shape gate.

Step 6 changes the diagnosis provenance contract but omits src/theforge/diagnose_types.py and its callers. SupportProvenance currently normalizes source_type to observed, prior_assertion, mixed, or unknown, which does not structurally distinguish target-source verification from attached-snapshot support; parsing, rendering, and audit serialization all consume that type.

Step 4 routes the shape-gate acceptance criterion through src/theforge/cli/forge_yaml_guard.py, which validates forge.yaml top-level key changes on story branches (_ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS, evaluate_forge_yaml_guard, cmd_check_story_config). It has no function that evaluates an issue title/body/labels. The real gate is the theforge.shape_check package — theforge.shape_check.check(title, body, labels, ...) in src/theforge/shape_check/check.py, with the heuristics that a filed bug body must survive (check_bug_missing_diagnosis, check_missing_acceptance_criteria, check_missing_example, check_implementation_plan_in_body, check_type_shape_contradiction). A dev following the plan as written would either modify an unrelated module or wire the wrong validator, and the criterion 'the filed body satisfies the target repository's shape gate at creation' has no correct named surface.

Carried from the plan's stated risk 2 (GitHub attachment mechanics). GitHub has no file-attachment API for issues — only issue body and comments, each capped at 65536 characters. The only existing helper is post_findings_comment in src/theforge/coordinator/github_integration.py; nothing in the repo uploads artifact payloads. Step 4's 'attach the serialized evidence bundle plus artifact payloads' therefore has no transport, and a full run log plus audit plus sprint state plus reviewer outputs will exceed a single comment for any real sprint. The mitigation ('reuse existing GitHub helper modules') locates a comment poster but does not decide how oversized payloads travel.

Step 1 says the collector captures 'the resolved configuration snapshot recorded for that run', but the snapshot forge actually persists is sprint-scoped: coordinator/config_snapshot.py writes .forge/sprints/<sprint_id>/forge.yaml plus config_snapshot.yaml (including drift events). A run id does not directly key it, and a run outside a sprint has no pin at all. Falling back to the observing project's live forge.yaml in that case would reproduce the exact wrong-runtime failure this story exists to eliminate.

Step 5's 'discover the attached bundle before falling back to local-path evidence' collides with how diagnose_evidence.py resolves references today: a 12-hex run/sprint id (_HEX_ID_RE) carries no namespace and is probed against the local checkout's .forge/ run-log glob and sprint dirs. A report body citing the observing project's run f5aa21cf2d8d could match a same-shaped local id, mixing wrong-runtime artifacts into the diagnosis — the namespace refusal the module already applies to bare #NNNN has no equivalent for hex ids.

Carried from the plan's stated risk 3 (target shape gate not evaluable locally). The gate ships inside the forge package, so forge report running in the observing project validates with that project's installed release, which by this story's own premise may lag the target repository's current gate. 'Fail closed if the gate cannot be evaluated' does not cover the case where it evaluates successfully against a stale rule set.

To prevent Markdown or YAML parsers from corrupting whitespace or carriage returns in attached run log files or candidate payloads, the evidence bundle should be serialized (e.g. via base64 encoding) inside the issue body's metadata container.

Residual of stated risk 3. Step 5 records the shape-gate version used and fails closed when validation cannot run, which covers the unevaluable case — but not the case where the observing project's older installed gate evaluates the body successfully against a stale rule set and the target repository's newer gate then rejects it at creation. The version stamp makes that diagnosable after the fact but nothing detects it at filing time.

Step 7 puts comment fetching in coordinator/diagnose_evidence.py and cli/diagnose.py, but the existing issue fetch used by the flow (diagnose_flow.py::_gh_fetch_issue) requests only number/title/body/state/labels. The plan does not say which of the two paths owns the comment query, so the dev could add a second gh round-trip on every diagnose invocation.

The stated stale-defaults risk is not retired. Step 1 reloads .forge/sprints/<id>/forge.yaml through the currently installed loader and calls resolved_config_payload(), but config_snapshot.py preserves only raw YAML. coordinator/audit.py::_build_configuration_block records only the actual resolved hash and explicitly notes that CLI overrides rebuild the runtime config. Raw YAML cannot recover omitted old-version defaults, CLI overrides, or environment-resolved values, so a later diagnosis still cannot answer configuration questions from the run's exact snapshot.

Step 1 locates the run log at .forge/logs/*/run-<id>.log, matching diagnose_evidence.py's current one-level glob. Sprint story logs are created by coordinator/log_tee.py under .forge/logs/<sprint-name>/<story-slug>/run-<id>.log, so the proposed collector predictably reports the required sprint run log missing even when it exists.

findings.description: The 8 acceptance criteria span two distinct concerns: (1) the filing/reporting pipeline — capturing forge version, config snapshot, and artifacts, satisfying the shape gate, and reporting missing evidence (ACs 1,2,3,4,7,8) — and (2) hardening forge diagnose itself to treat attached evidence as untrusted data and to distinguish verified-vs-snapshot-only claims (ACs 5,6). The first is a CLI/artifact-bundling feature reviewable against the reporting checkout; the second is a prompt-injection defense and reasoning-provenance change reviewable against the diagnosing checkout's agent behavior. A reviewer would need to evaluate an artifact-collection CLI and an LLM injection-resistance/verification mechanism as one PR, which are different risk profiles and different code paths.

stories.name: forge report: file a cross-project bug with bundled evidence
acs: A bug can be filed against a target repository from the project where it was observed in a single command, without hand-copying artifacts between checkouts.
The filed report carries the forge version that actually produced the behavior, not the version installed wherever the report is later read.
The filed report carries the failing run's resolved configuration as that run saw it.

The run artifacts a diagnosis needs travel with the report and are reachable by forge diagnose on the resulting issue: the run log, the per-story audit, the sprint state, the reviewer outputs for the run, the story body as of the run, and any intake candidate artifacts involved.
The filed body satisfies the target repository's shape gate at creation.
When some part of the evidence is unavailable for a referenced run, the report states which part is missing rather than filing a report that reads as complete.

stories.name: forge diagnose: treat attached cross-project evidence as untrusted data with verified-provenance reporting
acs: Attached evidence is treated as data. Content originating in another project's agent output never acts as instruction to the diagnosing agent.

A diagnosis built on attached evidence distinguishes claims verified against the target repository's source from claims resting only on the attached snapshot, so premise verification reports what it was unable to check rather than presenting both alike.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: `forge report --run <id> --to <owner/repo>`, run in the observing project. The run audit (`.forge/audits/runs/<run_id>.json`) is the spine — it already carries `forge_version`, `sprint_id`, `task` and `reviews`. One run-time gap is closed first and it is now a 3-line write, not a schema change: `_build_configuration_block` computes `resolved_config_sha256(config)` from the object the coordinator actually held (after CLI overrides), so beside it we write the matching payload to a CONTENT-ADDRESSED sidecar `.forge/audits/configs/<sha>.json.gz`. The digest is the filename, so payload and digest cannot disagree; identical configs across runs share one ~5KB file, so the per-run audit record does not grow at all. Everything travels as ONE gzip+base64 blob in a fenced block in the issue body — measured complete-config cost 7,944 chars. Read side is a new module `report_bundle.py`; `diagnose_evidence.py` is NOT TOUCHED.

steps.description: Persist each run's resolved configuration to a content-addressed sidecar, so a later diagnosis can read the values the run executed under.
steps.details: In `_build_configuration_block` (audit.py:1255), at the point `resolved_sha256` is successfully computed, also write `<project>/.forge/audits/configs/<resolved_sha256>.json.gz` containing `gzip(json.dumps(config_provenance.resolved_config_payload(config), sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')))`. Secrets are already redacted by that function (`_REDACTED_VALUE_PATHS`, provenance.py:55-64) — this adds no new redaction surface. Write-if-absent: the filename IS the digest, so an existing file is byte-identical by construction and rewriting it is pure cost. WHY A SIDECAR AND NOT A RECORD FIELD — the prior round's reviewer correctly noted that ~57KB inside every `.forge/audits/runs/*.json` inflates the whole tree. Content addressing makes it one file per distinct configuration, shared by every run under it. It also means NO `CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump, no `MIGRATION_HELPERS` entry, and no change to `audit_storage.py` or `test_audit_schema_guard.py`: the record's serialized shape is unchanged, and the pointer to the sidecar is the `resolved_sha256` that record already carries. Never raises — wrap in `except Exception` and continue, per the block's own stated "identity must never break audit emission" rule. A run whose sidecar write failed is indistinguishable from a legacy run downstream, which is correct: both mean "not captured", and step 2 reports both as UNAVAILABLE rather than reconstructing. Tests: sidecar written at the digest name and gunzips to the redacted payload; a config carrying a secret writes `<redacted>`; a CLI-override'd config writes the override, not the file value (the case raw pinned YAML provably cannot recover); an unwritable audits dir leaves the audit record intact and emitted.

steps.description: Collect, encode and decode the evidence bundle.
steps.details: One module owns both directions so the wire format has exactly one definition. `collect(run_id, project_root) -> Bundle`, `encode(Bundle) -> str`, `decode(issue_body) -> Bundle | None`, `render_prompt_block(Bundle) -> str`. COLLECTION — from the run audit: `forge_version` (the version that produced the behavior), `sprint_id`, `task` (story body as of the run), `reviews` (reviewer outputs). From `sprint_id`: `.forge/sprints/<id>/state.yaml`. From `run_id`: `.forge/intake/candidates`. Resolved config: read `.forge/audits/configs/<configuration.resolved_sha256>.json.gz` and carry it VERBATIM AND COMPLETE — never re-resolve the pinned `.forge/sprints/<id>/forge.yaml` through the installed loader, which resolves *this* release's defaults, cannot recover an older release's omitted ones, and cannot see the run's CLI overrides. When the sidecar is absent (legacy run, or step-1 write failure) the bundle records `resolved_config: {state: "unavailable", reason: "no snapshot captured for this run"}` and ships the pinned raw YAML separately, explicitly labelled raw-source-only and NOT the run's resolved values. LOG RESOLUTION — `log_tee.py:52` writes sprint story logs two levels deep (`.forge/logs/<sprint>/<slug>/run-<id>.log`) and standalone runs one level (`.forge/logs/<slug>/run-<id>.log`). Resolve through the audit's own sprint/story identity first, then a bounded both-depths fallback. A fixture MUST use the real two-level sprint layout — a one-level-only fixture passes while the sprint case, the only case this story exists for, reports its log missing. BUDGET — every artifact carries `complete` | `excerpted` | `missing(reason)` | `unavailable(reason)`; `missing` is never silently equivalent to absent. The resolved config is exempt from excerpting: it is carried whole or declared unavailable, never truncated, because a truncated config is where an absent key reads as a default — the exact wrong-runtime conclusion the spec cites. Artifacts are bounded with the existing per-kind discipline (log tail, file head) and fill the remaining budget in priority order. ENCODING — `base64(gzip(json.dumps(bundle, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')), 9))`, line-wrapped, inside a ```forge-report-bundle fence. `decode` gunzips, validates the carried `resolved_sha256` against a re-digest of the carried payload, and returns None (never a partial bundle) on any mismatch or corruption. Total encoded size is asserted under 45,000 chars, leaving >20,000 for prose within the 65,536 body limit. steps.description: Compose the report body and file it.

plan.approach: Add `forge report --run <id> --to <owner/repo>`, run in the observing project. It reads that project's existing run audit (`.forge/audits/runs/<run_id>.json`), which already records `forge_version`, `sprint_id`, `task` and `reviews`. One run-time gap is real and is closed first: the audit's configuration block records only `resolved_sha256`, so the run's resolved *values* are nowhere on disk. Raw pinned yaml cannot substitute — CLI overrides rebuild the config after load (`audit.py:_build_configuration_block` says so in its own comment) and an older release's defaults are unrecoverable from a file that omits them. So step 1 persists a redacted `resolved_payload` beside the digest that already exists, and the collector treats *that* as the only authoritative answer to a configuration question; legacy runs report resolved configuration UNAVAILABLE rather than reconstructing one. The bundle rides inside the filed issue body as a bounded fenced block, because `diagnose_evidence.build_starting_evidence` is already handed the issue body — so diagnose gains a parser, not a fetch path. Creation is gated by `admissibility.classify_admissibility()` against an explicitly-named *investigation-ready* contract the repo already publishes, and filed with report.py's own bounded `gh issue create --repo` subprocess.

steps.description: Persist the run's resolved configuration payload in the run audit, so a later diagnosis can answer configuration questions from the run's own values.
steps.details: `_build_configuration_block(config)` (audit.py:1255) already computes `config_provenance.resolved_config_sha256(config)` from the config object the coordinator actually held — after CLI overrides, after env resolution. Add one key beside it, `resolved_payload`, from `config_provenance.resolved_config_payload(config)` — the same input the digest is derived from, so the payload and the digest can never disagree, and secrets are already redacted by that function's `_REDACTED_VALUE_PATHS`. Guard it the same way the digest is: never raise, record `null` plus a `resolved_payload_error` string on failure, because identity must never break audit emission. `null` means "not captured", which is a claim the record must be able to make and which step 2 must not confuse with "captured as empty". This changes the record's serialized shape, so per ADR-0002 §"Schema versioning is load-bearing" it requires a `CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and a `MIGRATION_HELPERS` entry in `audit_storage.py`; the migration is a defaulting one (older records gain `resolved_payload: null`), and `tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py` is updated as the writer-side snapshot it is. Tests: payload present and redacted for a config carrying a secret; payload reflects a CLI override rather than the file value; capture failure records the error and leaves the rest of the block intact; an unmigrated legacy record reads back as `null`.

steps.description: Collect a bounded evidence bundle from the observing project's run artifacts.
steps.details: New stdlib+yaml module. `collect(run_id, project_root) -> ReportEvidence`. Read `.forge/audits/runs/<run_id>.json` as the spine: it already carries `forge_version` (the version that produced the behavior), `sprint_id`, `task` (the story as of the run) and `reviews` (reviewer outputs). From `sprint_id` reach `.forge/sprints/<id>/state.yaml`, the pinned `.forge/sprints/<id>/forge.yaml` and `config_snapshot.yaml`; from `run_id` reach `.forge/intake/candidates`. LOG RESOLUTION — do not copy `diagnose_evidence`'s one-level `.forge/logs/*/run-<id>.log` glob: `log_tee.py:52` writes sprint story logs to `.forge/logs/<sprint-name>/<story-slug>/run-<id>.log` (two levels) and standalone runs to `.forge/logs/<story-slug>/run-<id>.log` (one). Resolve through the audit's own sprint/story identity first, then fall back to a bounded lookup that covers both depths under `.forge/logs`. A fixture must use the real two-level sprint layout; a one-level-only fixture would pass while the sprint case — the only case this story exists for — reports its required log missing. CONFIG — the resolved view comes from the audit's `configuration.resolved_payload` and from nowhere else. It is never recomputed by loading the pinned yaml through the currently-installed loader: that loader resolves *this* release's defaults, cannot recover an older release's omitted ones, and cannot see the CLI overrides the run executed under. When `resolved_payload` is absent (a run predating step 1) or null, the bundle states `resolved configuration: UNAVAILABLE (run predates capture)` and ships the pinned raw yaml verbatim as raw-source-only evidence, explicitly labelled as not the run's resolved values. Reconstruct-and-present is the exact failure the spec describes, one layer over. Every artifact carries an explicit state: `complete`, `excerpted`, or `missing` with a reason; `missing` is never silently equivalent to absent. Reuse the excerpting discipline already in `diagnose_evidence` (log tail, file head, per-excerpt char cap) rather than inventing new bounds. The resolved payload is collected at highest priority against the shared budget, since configuration questions are the spec's named failure. Fixtures: a full run; a run missing its log; a run whose sprint dir has no pinned forge.yaml; a legacy run with no `resolved_payload` (asserting UNAVAILABLE, not a reconstruction); a pinned forge.yaml that fails to load — `load.py` raises `ValueError` on unknown keys at three sites (sandbox 140-144, models 222-226, validation.profiles 924-928), so a yaml pinned by a different release can fail outright; that degrades to the same shape as UNAVAILABLE with the load error as the reason, and never falls back to the live project config; and a run log larger than the per-excerpt cap, asserting state `excerpted` — distinct from both `complete` and `missing`, which is what keeps a truncated bundle from reading as complete.

steps.description: Name the investigation-ready creation contract in the admissibility module.
steps.details: Additive only — no change to existing behavior or to any current caller. Add `REPORT_ALLOWED_REFUSAL_CODES = frozenset({ShapeVerdict.DIAGNOSIS_CAUSE_UNKNOWN.value})` and `classify_report_readiness(title, body, labels) -> ReportReadiness`, a thin wrapper that calls `classify_admissibility()` and applies the two-outcome rule in `gate_contract` above, carrying through the underlying `Admissibility` so callers can report the real verdict and detail. This lives in `admissibility.py` because that module is already the single place the gate/queue disagreement is a code change rather than a drift; a report-side copy of the rule elsewhere would reintroduce exactly that drift. `shape_check/check.py`, `shape_check/heuristics.py` and `sprint/shape_gate.py` are read/call-only in this story — they have consumers well beyond it (intake/groom, intake/findings, cli/sprint, the shape_check Action) and need no change.

steps.description: Compose the report body and file it.
steps.details: `register_parser` + `cmd_report`, matching `cli/diagnose.py`'s shape, taking `--run`, `--to`, and the operator's description. Compose a `bug`-labelled body: a `## Diagnosis` section built from `diagnosis_spec.render_bug_skeleton_body()`'s labels (Observed symptom, Evidence, Confirmed cause, Affected code path, Fix-success criterion), with Confirmed cause defaulting to "not yet identified" unless the operator supplied one; then the evidence section from step 2 rendered inside a fenced block under a heading that is NOT an acceptance-criteria heading. Body layout is chosen to keep the gate green by construction, verified by test rather than by assertion: the `bug` label makes `is_bug_format_issue` true, which exempts `check_implementation_plan_in_body`, `check_criterion_needs_live_evidence` and `check_missing_example`; carrying no AC-pattern heading keeps `check_type_shape_contradiction` clean and leaves `check_too_many_behavioral_clusters` and `check_implementation_design_dump` inert (both require an AC section). One trap the evidence text must be scrubbed for: `check_superseded` scans the whole body including fenced regions, so an artifact excerpt containing "superseded by #N" would BLOCK the filing — neutralize that literal in collected content and test it. Validate the exact composed title/body/labels with `classify_report_readiness` before any network call; on refusal, print the verdict, description and detail and exit non-zero without creating anything. CREATION — there is no issue-creation helper in `coordinator/github_integration.py` (it defines only `assign_pr_reviewers` and `post_findings_comment`), so report.py owns its own bounded subprocess, following the real precedents at `cli/todo.py:31-95` (`_run_gh` with `capture_output`, `text`, `cwd`, `timeout=30`; non-zero return prints stderr and exits 1) and `advisory_conventions.py:466`. The command is `gh issue create --repo <owner/repo> --title <t> --body <b> --label bug` — neither precedent passes `--repo` today, and cross-repo targeting is precisely what this story adds. Tests assert the argv against a mocked subprocess, not against an imported helper. Print the local forge/shape-gate version used for validation to the operator's terminal as well as recording it in the body, with one line stating plainly that validation ran against the LOCAL gate, so a rejection at the target repository is attributable to gate skew without reopening the filed issue. The rendered evidence block states missing, excerpted and unavailable artifacts explicitly, so a partial bundle never reads as complete.

steps.description: Wire the command into the CLI.
steps.details: Import `report`, call `report.register_parser(subparsers)` and add `"report": report.cmd_report` to the dispatch table. `main.py` stays wiring only.

steps.description: Teach diagnose to read the embedded bundle and stop probing local artifacts for it.
steps.details: `build_starting_evidence` already receives `issue_body`, so no new `gh` call, no change to `diagnose_flow._gh_fetch_issue`, and no extra round-trip on issues carrying no bundle. Parse the fenced report block out of the body; when present, emit its artifacts as evidence items labelled as originating in the observing project, and suppress local `.forge/` probing of every hex id that appears inside that block. This is the module's existing namespace doctrine — "loading nothing is a correct outcome; loading same-numbered content from the wrong repository is not" — extended from bare `#NNNN` to foreign run/sprint ids, which are the same collision in a different id space. Test that a diagnosing checkout holding a same-named `.forge/logs/*/run-<id>.log` still serves the attached excerpt and never the local file. Bundle items count against the existing `_MAX_TOTAL_EVIDENCE_CHARS` budget like any other item.
